mainEntity.name: Why use Gojo instead of Apple Dictation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Gojo when explicit local speech-model choices, offline operation after model installation, and documented focus validation before insertion matter. Apple Dictation is the simpler free option for ordinary speech input.

blocks.label: Short answer
blocks.copy: Choose Apple Dictation for free, built-in speech input wherever you can type. Choose Gojo when you want to select and download a local Whisper or Parakeet model, keep the documented speech path offline after installation, and use dictation beside a MacBook notch workspace.

blocks.text: Apple's own on-device wording is deliberately specific

content.s: Apple says you can check Keyboard settings to see whether voice inputs and transcripts for general text Dictation, such as composing messages and notes, are processed on-device and not sent to Siri servers. Apple distinguishes that example from dictating in a search box. It also says Dictation availability and features vary by language and region.

That means the honest comparison is not that Apple Dictation is always cloud-based or always local. It is the free baseline with a status Apple asks users to verify in their own settings. If data handling is important, check that screen for the selected language and test the exact place where you plan to dictate.

blocks.text: Gojo puts the local choices in the product

content.s: Gojo exposes four explicit local speech-model downloads: Whisper Small, Whisper Large v3, Parakeet Unified, and Parakeet v3. The shortcut never starts a download. With a verified model installed, Gojo documents a local-only path, no cloud fallback, and a focus check before it inserts final text. These controls add setup work, microphone and Accessibility permissions, and a paid app to a job Apple already gives away.

items: Apple says Dictation can enter text anywhere you can type.

Apple says Dictation is not available in all languages or regions and feature availability varies.
